text.brief: In May 1892 the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association in San Francisco told Chinese residents across the country not to register under a new federal law that required them to carry a certificate of residence.
text.record: The Chinese Exclusion Act of May 6, 1882, suspended the entry of Chinese laborers and barred Chinese immigrants from naturalization. The Geary Act of 1892 extended the ban and required every Chinese laborer to carry a certificate of residence on pain of arrest and deportation. The Supreme Court upheld the certificate in Fong Yue Ting v. United States in 1893, and Congress repealed exclusion only in December 1943.
